data.title: Nissei ASB Freezes Japan Plant Plan Amid Construction Strains, Not Demand Slump
data.description:
Nissei ASB Machine Co,. Ltd. ( (JP:6284) ) has provided an announcement.

Nissei ASB Machine Co., Ltd. has moved to correct recent media reports suggesting that a planned plant in Saku City, Nagano Prefecture was frozen because of weakening demand for plastic container molding machines. The company stresses that global demand for its molding equipment remains strong, with business performance trending firmly, and cites its ongoing large-scale capital investment in its Indian plant as evidence of its strategy to meet expanding overseas orders.

Instead of a demand slowdown, Nissei ASB attributes the freeze of the Japanese plant project to sharp rises in construction material costs and prolonged building schedules due to labor shortages, which made the original timetable and budget unworkable. To avoid burdening Saku City and other stakeholders with an uncertain and delayed project, the company has requested a buyback of the land, emphasizing corporate social responsibility, and notes that the decision will not affect its consolidated earnings for the current fiscal year.

data.title: M Vest Water lifts revenues and deepens NORWAFLOC® footprint despite Middle East delay
data.description:
M Vest Water AS ( (DE:7YA) ) has issued an announcement.

M Vest Water reported first-half 2026 revenues of NOK 15.7 million, with Q2 sales of NOK 9.9 million, a 27% year-on-year increase driven by strong chemical sales and higher NORWAFLOC® volumes. Chemical revenues in the second quarter rose 36% from a year earlier, underscoring momentum in core product demand across aquaculture and industrial water treatment.

Aquaculture has emerged as a profitable standalone segment with strong earnings visibility, supported by the company’s largest salmon slaughterhouse customer ramping consumption of NORWAFLOC® in the second half of 2026. The company is targeting annual turnover of NOK 100–150 million from aquaculture between 2028 and 2030, signaling an ambition to scale this vertical significantly within its overall growth strategy.

The company also achieved a key milestone at METHA, one of Europe’s largest dredging plants, where a long-term pilot showed NORWAFLOC® improves treatment performance and operational efficiency, paving the way for commercial negotiations. Existing industrial customer SAR increased NORWAFLOC® consumption at its Mongstad water treatment plant, boosting recurring product volumes and reinforcing the customer’s environmental commitment.

Its non-toxic, biodegradable products are designed to deliver high purification efficiency with minimal environmental impact. The firm’s portfolio includes proprietary chemicals such as NORWAFLOC®, which are used in aquaculture, dredging, and industrial wastewater facilities. data.title: Sensirion rolls out long-life formaldehyde sensor for global indoor air quality market
data.description:
Sensirion Holding AG ( (CH:SENS) ) has shared an update.

Sensirion has launched worldwide availability of its SFA40 miniaturized electrochemical formaldehyde sensor, targeting integration into air purifiers, air conditioners and indoor air quality monitoring devices via its global distribution network. Designed for real-world environments, the sensor offers high selectivity for formaldehyde with minimal cross-sensitivity to common indoor gases, delivering accurate measurements in complex mixed-gas conditions.

Combining low energy consumption, a compact form factor and a lifetime of more than six years, the SFA40 supports energy-efficient, battery-powered devices and reliable long-term indoor air quality monitoring. Factory calibration in Switzerland, digital I²C output and anti-drying technology simplify integration and enhance stability, while sensitivity below key WHO, WELL Building Standard and Chinese GB/T 18883-2022 limits strengthens Sensirion’s position in the growing market for health-focused building and consumer air quality solutions.

data.title: Woojin I & S Calls Extraordinary Meeting to Tighten Governance and Boost Shareholder Returns
data.description:

Woojin I & S Co., Ltd. has called an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders for October 8, 2026 in Seoul to vote on shareholder‑driven changes to its governance and capital policies, including amending its Articles of Incorporation to require an annually disclosed shareholder value enhancement plan. The board materials show active engagement by independent directors and ongoing investments and financing activities in semiconductor‑related and general facilities businesses, underscoring the firm’s positioning in a cyclical yet technologically evolving construction market.

Key agenda items include approval of a sizeable treasury share acquisition of up to KRW 7.5 billion and the retirement of 517,530 existing treasury shares, which would cut total outstanding shares and are framed as measures to bolster shareholder value and stabilize the share price.
